description:
FILED s538 (reviewing session, 2026-11-10) from a review probe of s536i (#4685: "every backslash spelling goes through _backslash_lvalue_form with the scalar() unwrap").  PRE-EXISTING: main 4a39a1c7 copies in EVERY spelling below; the s536i tree (88108e97) fixes all but the two parenthesised ones.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3; probe files ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s538/review/i/p3b.pl + .perl/.main/.tree):

    my @a = (5,6); my $x = 1;
    my $r2 = \(scalar($a[0])); $$r2 = 72; print "@a\n";   # perl 72 6     s536i tree: 5 6
    my $r3 = \(scalar($x));    $$r3 = 73; print "$x\n";   # perl 73       s536i tree: 1

RIGHT on the s536i tree: `\scalar($a[1])`, `\scalar($h{k})`, `\scalar($ar->[1])`, `\scalar($$ar[0])`, and the LIST form `\(scalar($x), $a[0])`.  So the miss is the ONE-element paren list `\( scalar(X) )` only.

SUSPECT (not measured): the paren arm of the backslash lowering in Pl/ExprToCL.pm handles a one-element list before `_backslash_lvalue_form` sees the `scalar()` operand, or the k=1 paren is folded away so the operand arrives as an rvalue funcall.  The cheap discriminating measurement: `./pl2cl` on the two lines and read which head the `\(...)` emits beside the working `\scalar($x)` -- it was not taken here because the batch that owns the function (s536i) is on its final legs and the tree must not move under them.

Fix shape: route the one-element paren through the same unwrap (ONE path, rule 11), never a third copy.  Probe the breaking shapes: `\(scalar(@a))` (a ref to the COUNT, a temporary), `\(scalar(f()))`, `\(my $y)`, `\(@a)` (a list of element refs).  Bar: guard rows in Pl/t/lvalue-ref-01.t that fail on the base; corpus-diff + wide A/B.
subject: `\(scalar($x))` -- a PARENTHESISED backslash of scalar(SCALAR / element) references a COPY; perl references the operand (#4685 residue)
